page.description: Overview and management of the built-in punch clock. Employees set to "System punch" clock in from their portal; external import can coexist, distinguished by each employee's attendance source.

card.title: Clock In / Out
card.stateOpen: Currently clocked in; the next punch is "Clock Out"
card.stateIdle: Not clocked in; the next punch is "Clock In"
card.ipBlocked: Your current network ({{ip}}) is not allowed for punching. Please connect to the company network.
card.devicePending: This device is awaiting HR approval before you can punch.
card.deviceRevoked: This device's binding was revoked. Please contact HR.
card.deviceOther: This device is bound to another employee and cannot be used to punch.
card.deviceNew: This is a new device; it will be registered to your account on your first punch.

today.empty: No employees use system punch yet. Change their attendance source to "System punch" in Settings or the employee profile.

events.voidHint: Voiding does not delete: the original record is kept with who voided it and why, and the daily attendance is recomputed from the remaining valid records.
events.reasonPlaceholder: Required, e.g. pressed clock-out by mistake; forgot to punch, confirmed by manager
events.correctionHint: HR can add a punch when an employee forgot to. Only for employees using system punch; a reason is required and future times are not allowed.

devices.hint: Each browser has a random ID registered to one employee; a device cannot punch for two people. This is browser-level binding (web pages cannot read hardware MAC addresses). Pending devices also count toward the employee's device limit.
devices.label: Device

settings.networkHint: One IPv4 address or CIDR range per line. Leave empty for no restriction.
settings.networkNote: IPv4 only. Field staff can be exempted in their employee profile. Make sure the IP the system sees is your company's outbound IP (watch out behind reverse proxies or container networks).
settings.deviceHint: Prevents punching for someone else: each employee can only use devices registered to them.
settings.modeFlag: Flag only: allow punching but mark anomalies
settings.autoApproveHint: The device used for an employee's first punch is bound automatically; later devices need HR approval.
settings.macNote: Why not bind MAC addresses? Browsers do not let web pages read them, the server only sees IPs, and phones randomize MACs, so a browser ID is used instead. It cannot stop someone remotely controlling the employee's own computer.
settings.shiftHint: For days without a schedule, fixed-schedule employees use this shift to detect late arrival and early leave (grace minutes follow the existing setting); a schedule takes precedence. Break time is used by the working-hours alerts.
settings.sourceHint: Switch employees' attendance source by department to pilot department by department. Employees switched to "System punch" are skipped by external attendance imports.

exceptions.title: Missed Punches
exceptions.description: Automatically detects employees who were supposed to work but did not punch fully (by schedule, or by default shift and calendar for fixed-schedule employees without one) and notifies HR. Approved leave and outings are not counted.

compliance.title: Actual punch compliance
compliance.description: After-the-fact checks on actual punches: daily hours, consecutive days, monthly overtime. Scheduling rules (rest between shifts, days off) are now checked live on the Schedule page. An aid, not a legal ruling.

requests.correctionHint: On approval a punch is added automatically (with the request number and approver) and the daily attendance is updated.
requests.outingHint: Approved days are not counted as missed punches, and the employee may punch outside the allowed network that day.

extras.noSchedule: No published schedule for the coming days.
extras.correctionDescription: If you forgot to punch, submit a request; once your manager or HR approves it, it is added automatically. Only the last 31 days.
extras.outingDescription: Request before an outing or business trip. Approved days are not counted as missed punches, and you may punch outside the company network.
extras.destinationPlaceholder: e.g. Training at a client site

stats.sinceNote: Blocked punch attempts have been recorded since {{since}}; earlier ones were not recorded, so earlier periods look lower.
stats.noRejectionsYet: No blocked punch attempts recorded yet.

charts.blockedHint: IP not allowed, device not approved or bound to someone else
charts.qualityHint: Detected misses, employee correction requests, HR corrections

stats.byCodeHint: Includes operational mistakes (double clock-in, clock-out without clock-in); those are not protection issues
stats.topIpsHint: Homes, phone hotspots and other sites show up here; widely scattered sources mean more people punch outside the company network
stats.topEmployeesHint: Find out whether there is a legitimate reason (field work, forgot an outing request) before treating it as fraud
stats.readTitle: How to read this (deciding on QR codes or location)
stats.readHint: These numbers are for reference only and draw no automatic conclusion. Collect one to two months first.

read.ip: High IP-blocked share: look at the sources first. If concentrated in a few people or IPs, it is usually field staff without an outing request or a missing site in the allowlist — fix the rules or exempt them. Widely scattered sources (homes, hotspots) combined with a need to prove on-site presence is the reason to consider QR codes.
read.device: Many device blocks: "bound to another employee" means someone used another person's or a shared device — find out why; many "new device awaiting approval" is usually a process issue (new phone, cleared browser data), not fraud.
read.quality: Many missed punches and corrections: mostly reminder or process issues, not fraud, and QR codes would not fix them; check for missing schedules or unfiled outings first.
read.decision: If all of these are low, the existing IP restriction plus device binding is enough and adds no maintenance cost. If many punches happen off-network and fraud is a concern, then evaluate QR codes (web GPS can be spoofed and is not recommended as a safeguard).
